# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

**How to use this:** Work through rooms in the order listed. Earlier rooms contain things you use least, so they can be packed first. Each room has a declutter pass built in — do it before you pack, not during, or you'll slow down. Label every box with the room name and a 1–3 word content summary (e.g., "Kitchen — baking tools").

---

## 1. Storage / Garage / Attic

**Responsible:** J | **Priority:** Start first (weeks 6–5) | **Estimated time:** 4–8 hours depending on volume

**Declutter first:**
This is where the most cuttable weight lives. Be aggressive. If you haven't touched it since the last move, it probably shouldn't survive this one. Seasonal gear you won't need in Oregon's climate (heavy snow blower, for instance) can go. Rusty or duplicate tools, old paint cans, and broken items should be tossed, donated, or recycled. Take photos of anything you're unsure about — if you wouldn't buy it again today for half its price, let it go.

**Pack:**
- [ ] Seasonal decorations (holiday, outdoor)
- [ ] Camping, hiking, and outdoor gear
- [ ] Tools and hardware (wrap sharp edges, bag small parts and label them)
- [ ] Sporting equipment
- [ ] Luggage and travel bags (use suitcases as packing containers for heavy items like books)
- [ ] Stored furniture, shelving, or bins
- [ ] Lawn and garden tools — decide what's worth the weight
- [ ] Car supplies (jumper cables, emergency kit — set the emergency kit aside for the drive)

---

## 2. Guest Room / Spare Room / Office

**Responsible:** P (office items), J (guest room) | **Priority:** Weeks 5–4 | **Estimated time:** 3–5 hours

**Declutter first:**
Shred old paperwork you don't need (keep tax returns for 7 years, vital records forever). Recycle old magazines, manuals for products you no longer own, and outdated tech cables. Donate books you won't reread. Old electronics can go to an e-waste drop-off.

**Pack:**
- [ ] Books (small boxes, spines down, fill gaps with packing paper)
- [ ] Desk supplies, stationery, and office equipment
- [ ] Computer peripherals and cables (label both ends of each cable or take a photo of the back of your setup before unplugging)
- [ ] Files and documents — separate "carry with us" documents (see the master list) from "ship" files
- [ ] Guest bedding, pillows, and towels (use vacuum bags to compress)
- [ ] Art, frames, and wall décor (cardboard corner protectors, wrap in bubble wrap, pack upright)
- [ ] Printer, scanner, monitor (original boxes if you have them; otherwise double-wrap and mark FRAGILE)

---

## 3. Living Room / Family Room

**Responsible:** J | **Priority:** Weeks 4–3 | **Estimated time:** 4–6 hours

**Declutter first:**
DVDs, CDs, and games you've replaced digitally can be donated or sold. Old remotes, dead batteries, mystery chargers, and tangled cables in the junk drawer — toss them. Decorative items you don't love enough to wrap, protect, and carry 2,400 miles should stay behind.

**Pack:**
- [ ] Books and media (small boxes)
- [ ] Decorative items, vases, candles, and knickknacks (wrap individually)
- [ ] Throw pillows, blankets, and curtains (vacuum bags or garbage bags)
- [ ] Electronics: TV, sound bar, gaming consoles, streaming devices. Take photos of cable setups. Wrap screens in moving blankets or towels, not bubble wrap (it can leave marks on warm screens)
- [ ] Lamps (remove bulbs and shades, wrap shades in paper, pack bulbs separately)
- [ ] Board games, puzzles, and hobby items
- [ ] Small furniture drawers — if the mover allows it, leave clothes in dresser drawers and wrap the dresser. If DIY, tape drawers shut
- [ ] Area rugs (roll tightly, secure with rope or stretch wrap)

---

## 4. Dining Room

**Responsible:** P | **Priority:** Weeks 4–3 | **Estimated time:** 2–3 hours

**Declutter first:**
Chipped dishes, mismatched glasses, placemats you never use, and the fondue set from 2016 can all go. Keep only the servingware you actually put on a table in the last year.

**Pack:**
- [ ] China, glassware, and stemware (pack vertically like records, not flat-stacked; use cell dividers or wrap each piece in paper)
- [ ] Serving dishes and platters (paper between each layer)
- [ ] Table linens, placemats, napkins
- [ ] Candlesticks and centerpieces
- [ ] Buffet or hutch contents
- [ ] Small appliances stored in the dining area (wrap cords, bag accessories)

---

## 5. Kitchen

**Responsible:** J | **Priority:** Weeks 3–2 (non-essentials) and final 2 days (essentials) | **Estimated time:** 6–10 hours total — this is usually the longest room

**Declutter first:**
The kitchen is the single best place to cut weight and box count. Duplicate spatulas, novelty mugs, stained plastic containers without lids, expired spices and food, single-use gadgets (melon baller, avocado slicer), and anything you bought "just in case" — donate or discard. Keep one good version of each tool. If you have more than 8 mugs for a 2-person household, choose your favorites.

**Pack in two waves:**

*Wave 1 — weeks 3–2 (things you won't need):*
- [ ] Baking supplies and specialty pans
- [ ] Entertaining dishes, punch bowls, extra serving ware
- [ ] Cookbooks
- [ ] Small appliances you won't use in the next 2 weeks (stand mixer, blender, food processor, waffle maker)
- [ ] Vases, decorative items on top of cabinets
- [ ] Spice duplicates and pantry overflow

*Wave 2 — last 2 days:*
- [ ] Everyday dishes, cups, and silverware (keep one set per person until the last meal)
- [ ] Pots, pans, and cooking utensils
- [ ] Coffeemaker (pack the morning of moving day, right after the last pot)
- [ ] Cleaning supplies under the sink — keep a small kit out for final cleanup
- [ ] Refrigerator and freezer contents: use coolers for the drive, donate or toss the rest
- [ ] Trash bags, paper towels, and hand soap — these go in the car, not the truck

---

## 6. Bedrooms (Master and Any Others)

**Responsible:** Each person packs their own; J for shared items | **Priority:** Weeks 3–2 (off-season and extras), last 2 days (daily use) | **Estimated time:** 3–5 hours per bedroom

**Declutter first:**
Clothes are heavy and take up enormous space. Try the "reverse hanger" trick if time allows: turn all hangers backward and only flip them when you wear something. Anything still backward in two weeks gets donated. Worn-out shoes, old undergarments, and clothes that don't fit can go now. Under-bed storage often holds forgotten items — sort before you pack.

**Pack in two waves:**

*Wave 1 — weeks 3–2:*
- [ ] Off-season clothing (vacuum bags save a lot of space)
- [ ] Shoes you won't wear in the next 2 weeks (stuff shoes with socks to hold shape, pack in original boxes or wrap in paper)
- [ ] Extra bedding, pillows, and linens
- [ ] Jewelry and accessories (carry valuables with you, not in the truck)
- [ ] Dresser décor, bedside items you don't use daily
- [ ] Luggage (use as packing containers)

*Wave 2 — last 2 days:*
- [ ] Daily clothes, sleepwear, and shoes (pack enough for 3–4 days of travel in a suitcase that stays in the car)
- [ ] Bedding you're sleeping on (strip and pack the morning of)
- [ ] Alarm clocks, phone chargers, and bedside essentials
- [ ] Hangers (bundle with rubber bands or pack in wardrobe boxes)

---

## 7. Bathrooms

**Responsible:** Each person handles their own toiletries; J for shared/linen closet | **Priority:** Last 3 days (non-essentials), morning of (daily items) | **Estimated time:** 1–2 hours per bathroom

**Declutter first:**
Expired medications (take to a pharmacy drop-off, don't flush), nearly-empty bottles, old makeup and skincare, ratty towels, and hotel shampoo collections. Medicine cabinets are graveyards — clear them out.

**Pack:**
- [ ] Towels and washcloths (keep 1 per person plus 1 for the dog; use extras as packing material for fragile items)
- [ ] Linen closet overflow (sheets, first aid supplies, extra TP — toss what's nearly gone)
- [ ] Hair tools, styling products (bag liquids in zip-lock bags to prevent leaks)
- [ ] Medications and vitamins (carry current prescriptions in the car, not the truck)
- [ ] Shower curtain, rings, bath mat (pack the morning of after final showers)
- [ ] Toiletries bag for the drive (toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, contacts, glasses — this goes in the car)

---

## 8. Laundry Room / Mudroom / Entry

**Responsible:** M | **Priority:** Last 3 days | **Estimated time:** 1–2 hours

**Declutter first:**
Old cleaning products, dried-up supplies, wire hangers, single gloves, and broken umbrellas.

**Pack:**
- [ ] Washer and dryer: run a cleaning cycle, disconnect hoses, let the washer drum dry 24 hours. Tape the drum (some models need shipping bolts reinstalled — check your manual or search your model number online)
- [ ] Iron, ironing board, drying rack
- [ ] Coats, boots, rain gear (keep what you need for travel weather)
- [ ] Cleaning supplies: keep a small "last clean" kit (all-purpose cleaner, paper towels, broom, dustpan, trash bags, toilet cleaner). This is the very last thing packed
- [ ] Pet leashes, harnesses, and outdoor gear stored here (set aside travel items for the car)

---

## 9. Outdoor / Patio / Balcony

**Responsible:** M | **Priority:** Weeks 3–2 | **Estimated time:** 1–3 hours

**Declutter first:**
Cheap resin furniture, rusty grills, cracked planters, and hose attachments that leak are not worth moving cross-country. Sell or give away patio furniture if you can replace it for less than the shipping weight cost.

**Pack:**
- [ ] Patio furniture (clean, fold, wrap cushions in plastic)
- [ ] Grill (clean, disconnect propane — propane tanks cannot go in a moving truck; dispose or give away). Pack grill tools separately
- [ ] Planters and garden décor
- [ ] Hoses, sprinklers, garden tools worth keeping
- [ ] Outdoor toys, bikes (deflate tires slightly for altitude changes on the drive)

---

# 6–8 Week Calendar of Reminders

**How to use this:** Each entry below has a short title suitable for a phone calendar event, a suggested date relative to your move day ("M-Day"), and a brief note. Set each as an all-day event or a morning reminder. Adjust dates if your timeline shifts. If your move day is a Saturday, count backward.

I'm using **M** to mean Move Day. So **M−42** means 42 days (6 weeks) before the move.

---

**M−56 (8 weeks out)**
Title: **Get moving quotes**
Note: Request 3–4 mover estimates or book DIY truck. Compare full-service, hybrid, and DIY.

**M−54**
Title: **Give landlord written notice**
Note: Send via email and certified mail. Keep a copy. Confirm your required notice period.

**M−50**
Title: **Vet visit — dog travel prep**
Note: Health check, updated vaccines, copy of all records, discuss travel anxiety meds if needed.

**M−49**
Title: **Start Oregon housing search**
Note: Set alerts on rental sites. Check dog breed and weight policies. Budget for deposits.

---

**M−42 (6 weeks out)**
Title: **Book mover or truck**
Note: Confirm date, get written estimate, pay deposit. Read the contract and valuation coverage.

**M−40**
Title: **Order packing supplies**
Note: Boxes, tape, bubble wrap, markers, vacuum bags. Ask stores for free boxes too.

**M−39**
Title: **Begin declutter — garage and storage**
Note: Donate, sell, or toss. Schedule a donation pickup or drop-off.

---

**M−35 (5 weeks out)**
Title: **Book vehicle shipping (if applicable)**
Note: Confirm open vs. enclosed, pickup window, and payment.

**M−33**
Title: **Pack storage, garage, and attic**
Note: First rooms to pack. Label every box with room and contents.

**M−32**
Title: **Plan driving route and book hotels**
Note: Dog-friendly stops every 2–3 hrs. Book pet-friendly lodging for each overnight.

---

**M−28 (4 weeks out)**
Title: **Pack guest room and office**
Note: Shred old papers, label cables, back up computer files.

**M−27**
Title: **Sign Oregon lease / confirm housing**
Note: Save lease to your Move folder. Confirm move-in date and key pickup.

**M−26**
Title: **Schedule Oregon internet install**
Note: Often needs 2+ week lead time. Book now.

**M−25**
Title: **Start USPS change of address**
Note: Go to usps.com. Set the forwarding start date to your move day.

---

**M−21 (3 weeks out)**
Title: **Pack living room and dining room**
Note: Photos of cable setups. Wrap fragile items individually.

**M−20**
Title: **Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs**
Note: Electric, gas, water, trash. Set end dates for the day after the move.

**M−19**
Title: **Schedule Oregon utility startups**
Note: Electric, gas, water, internet. Set start dates for your arrival day.

**M−18**
Title: **Notify banks, insurance, and subscriptions**
Note: Update billing addresses. See the services list.

---

**M−14 (2 weeks out)**
Title: **Pack kitchen Wave 1**
Note: Baking, specialty items, cookbooks, small appliances you won't use.

**M−13**
Title: **Pack bedrooms Wave 1**
Note: Off-season clothes, extra bedding, shoes, luggage.

**M−12**
Title: **Confirm mover details**
Note: Arrival window, crew size, payment method, final estimate in writing.

**M−11**
Title: **Car maintenance check**
Note: Oil, tires, brakes, fluids, battery. Top off everything for a 2,400-mile drive.

**M−10**
Title: **Sell/donate remaining items**
Note: Schedule pickups. Post on local buy-nothing groups or marketplace.

---

**M−7 (1 week out)**
Title: **Pack bathrooms (non-essentials)**
Note: Keep 1 towel each, travel toiletries, and daily meds out.

**M−6**
Title: **Photograph valuables and serial numbers**
Note: Save to phone and a USB drive. Keep the drive in your documents folder.

**M−5**
Title: **Assemble moving-day car kit**
Note: Documents, meds, dog supplies, toiletries, chargers, snacks, water, cleaning kit. See the one-pager.

Title: **Defrost fridge

# Calendar Continued: M−4 Through Post-Move

---

**M−4**
Title: **Defrost fridge and freezer**
Note: Unplug, towel the floor, donate perishables. Clean interior once thawed.

**M−3**
Title: **Pack kitchen Wave 2 and bedrooms Wave 2**
Note: Keep 1 plate, 1 mug, 1 fork per person until tomorrow. Pack the rest.

**M−2**
Title: **Final laundry and last clean prep**
Note: Wash everything. Set aside travel clothes for 3–4 days. Prep the cleaning kit for move-out.

**M−1 (night before)**
Title: **Final pack and load car kit**
Note: Strip beds, pack last towels. Load the car with documents, dog bag, toiletries, snacks, cleaning kit, and suitcases. Charge all devices. Get sleep.

**M−1 (evening reminder)**
Title: **Confirm mover arrival time**
Note: Call or text the crew lead. Confirm address, parking, elevator, and payment method.

---

**M-Day (morning)**
Title: **MOVING DAY — morning tasks**
Note: Last coffee, pack the coffeemaker. Final walkthrough photos of every room and closets. Meter reads and photos. Dog in crate or secure room away from crew.

**M-Day (before leaving)**
Title: **MOVING DAY — lockup**
Note: Return keys, garage remotes, and fobs. Get a receipt. Do the final clean with your kit. Check every closet, cabinet, and the dishwasher. Sign the Bill of Lading only after reviewing it. Take your cleaning kit — toss it at the first gas station if you don't want to keep it.

**M-Day (on the road)**
Title: **Drive — first stop at 2 hours**
Note: Dog walk, water, and stretch. Log mileage and fuel receipts. Keep the documents folder accessible, not buried in the trunk.

---

**M+1**
Title: **Arrive or continue drive**
Note: If multi-day drive, repeat 2-hour dog breaks. Check in to lodging early if possible so the dog can settle.

**M+2**
Title: **Move-in day — document everything**
Note: Photograph every room, appliance, and any existing damage before unloading. Send photos to landlord in writing. Confirm utilities are on. Locate breaker box, water shutoff, and gas shutoff.

**M+5**
Title: **Oregon DMV — license and registration**
Note: Bring current license, proof of residency, vehicle title, insurance, and payment. Check whether you need an emissions test for your county.

**M+7 (1 week after)**
Title: **Dog — vet visit and license**
Note: First Oregon vet appointment. Transfer records. Ask about county or city dog license requirements. Update microchip registry.

**M+7**
Title: **Update address — round 2**
Note: Catch anything you missed: pharmacy, dentist, subscriptions, loyalty programs, voter registration, employer payroll.

**M+10**
Title: **Confirm Ohio deposit return**
Note: Check with former landlord on security deposit timeline. Ohio law generally requires return within 30 days; keep your forwarding address on file.

**M+14 (2 weeks after)**
Title: **Cancel Ohio car registration**
Note: Once Oregon plates are in hand, cancel Ohio registration and return plates if required by Ohio BMV.

**M+14**
Title: **Check all subscriptions and services**
Note: Verify nothing is still billing at the Ohio address. Confirm Oregon internet, utilities, and renter's insurance are active and correct.

**M+30**
Title: **Settle-in check**
Note: File moving receipts. Confirm deposit return from Ohio. Set a tax reminder to file part-year returns for both states. Breathe — you did it.

---

# Printable One-Page Moving Day Essentials

What follows is designed to be copied, pasted into a document, and printed on a single page. Keep it in the glovebox or the front seat.

---

**MOVING DAY CAR KIT — OHIO → OREGON**

**Documents (one folder, front seat)**

- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports
- [ ] Vehicle title, registration, and insurance cards
- [ ] Lease or closing papers (both homes)
- [ ] Moving contract, Bill of Lading, and inventory sheet
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact (if applicable)
- [ ] Dog: rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, vet contact
- [ ] Prescriptions list and insurance policy numbers
- [ ] Cash and one credit card easily accessible

**Valuables (carry, don't ship)**

- [ ] Laptops, tablets, external hard drives
- [ ] Jewelry and irreplaceable items
- [ ] Medications (all current prescriptions and a 2-week supply of each)
- [ ] Glasses, contacts, and contact solution
- [ ] USB drive with photos of valuables and serial numbers

**Personal bags (1 suitcase each, 3–4 days of clothes)**

- [ ] Changes of clothes, sleepwear, underwear, socks
- [ ] Comfortable driving shoes and walking shoes
- [ ] Light jacket or layers (mountain passes get cold)
- [ ] Toiletries bag: toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, shampoo, razor
- [ ] Phone chargers and car charger
- [ ] Headphones and entertainment for the passenger

**Dog bag**

- [ ] Food (enough for travel plus 3 extra days), portable bowls
- [ ] Water bottle and collapsible water bowl
- [ ] Leash, harness, collar with current ID tag
- [ ] Poop bags
- [ ] Favorite toy and familiar blanket or bed
- [ ] Crate or car seatbelt harness
- [ ] Calming aids or vet-prescribed travel medication
- [ ] Paper towels and enzyme cleaner for accidents
- [ ] Recent photo of dog on phone (in case of separation)

**Car emergency kit**

- [ ] Jumper cables or portable jump starter
- [ ] Tire pressure gauge and portable air compressor
- [ ] Flashlight and extra batteries
- [ ] Basic tool kit (screwdriver, pliers, wrench)
- [ ] First aid kit
- [ ] Blanket
- [ ] Reflective triangles or road flares
- [ ] Spare tire, jack, and lug wrench (confirm they're in the car)

**Snacks and comfort**

- [ ] Cooler with water, drinks, and cold snacks
- [ ] Non-perishable snacks (granola bars, nuts, crackers, dried fruit)
- [ ] Paper towels and wet wipes
- [ ] Trash bag
- [ ] Sunglasses
- [ ] Pillow for passenger naps

**Last-out cleaning kit (toss after final walkthrough)**

- [ ] All-purpose cleaner spray
- [ ] Roll of paper towels
- [ ] Trash bags
- [ ] Broom or Swiffer
- [ ] Toilet cleaner and brush (disposable)

**Before you pull away — final checks**

- [ ] Walkthrough photos and video of every room, closet, and exterior: done
- [ ] Meter reads photographed: done
- [ ] Keys, remotes, and fobs returned and receipt collected: done
- [ ] Bill of Lading reviewed and signed: done
- [ ] Dog secured in crate or harness: done
- [ ] Phone charged, GPS loaded with route and first stop: done
- [ ] Gas tank full: done

**Emergency contacts for the road**

- Moving company: _______________
- Vehicle shipping carrier: _______________
- Oregon landlord or realtor: _______________
- Vet (current): _______________
- Vet (Oregon): _______________
- Roadside assistance: _______________
- Emergency vet along route: _______________

---
